title: The refinement map on the localizing category
statement:
Work in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$; all schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible coefficient as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]: a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite in the fixed algebraic closure, with the indicated discrete or $\ell$-adic topology. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the unbounded module-object derived category, with the fixed universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use $\Dctf$ and its ambient localizing closure as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] and [sk-def-localizing-closure], and the module operations [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type. Let $X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{q}Y$ and $X\xrightarrow{j'}Z'\xrightarrow{q'}Y$ be dense compactifications of $f$ in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]: $j,j'$ are quasi-compact open immersions, $q,q'$ are proper, and $j,j'$ are scheme-theoretically dense. Let $h:Z'\to Z$ be a refinement, namely a proper $Y$-morphism such that $h\circ j'=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(X))=j'(X)$, identified with $X$ via $j,j'$. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ let
$$\theta_{h,K}:j^*Rh_*j'_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$$
be the canonical open-restriction isomorphism (restriction of direct image to $X$, followed by the inverse of the open-extension unit), and let $e_{h,K}:j_!K\to Rh_*j'_!K$ be adjoint to $\theta_{h,K}^{-1}$ under $j_!\dashv j^*$. Then:

1. $e_{h,K}$ is the unique map whose restriction to $X$ is the identity of $K$, meaning $\theta_{h,K}\circ j^*(e_{h,K})\circ\eta_{j,K}=\operatorname{id}_K$, where $\eta_j:\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!$ is the unit.
2. $e_{h,K}$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in\operatorname{Loc}(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$.
3. $e_{\operatorname{id},K}=\operatorname{id}$ under the canonical identity identifications. For successive refinements $Z''\xrightarrow{a}Z'\xrightarrow{h}Z$, with open $j'':X\to Z''$, one has $e_{ha,K}=Rh_*(e_{a,K})\circ e_{h,K}$ under the canonical derived-composition isomorphism $R(ha)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*Ra_*$, for every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The canonical module direct-image identity is the source lowerStarId with the same abelian components. Its linearity follows from the existing module identity and faithfulness of the forgetful functor gives naturality. Use the proved openUnitIsIso and exact derived adjunction to obtain the invertible open unit. The cartesianDerivedCounit in ExchangeMono, followed by conjugation of adjunctions, proves the existing open restriction comparison invertible for all unbounded complexes. Its equality with the specified map is the explicit mate calculation restrictionMate_isIso.

source.place: The restriction to X; exact adjunction and restriction comparison, retaining the existing canonical definitions.

proof.text: Adjunction.homEquiv identifies b with the unit followed by restriction of b. Cancel the invertible theta to show that the normalization equation is equivalent to this adjoint being theta inverse. Injectivity and the inverse identities of the equivalence give the stated iff. This proves uniqueness for every unbounded K.

Apply the single-compactification theorem to j and the compactification (jprime,h). All structural hypotheses follow from the compactification over-k instances, quasi-compactness of the distinguished opens, and properness of h. Thus F=Rh_*jprime_! preserves each ambient discrete sum whose vertices belong to Loc(Dctf). The exact inverse image V to the closed complement is a left adjoint on the derived categories, so V F preserves those same sums.

Classify the admissible coefficient into the standard properOpenInterchange disjunction or the separate all-continuous-map algebraic-closure case. For a finite coefficient ring in Type 0, construct the coefficient isomorphism to its universe lift sectionwise by postcomposition with ULift.up/down; its ring structure is pointwise, so it lifts to a monoid-object isomorphism. The annihilating power of ell is unchanged. The valuation and finite-field presentations agree definitionally with their named continuous presentations. For the standard disjunction, apply properOpenInterchange to p=id_X and the compactification (jprime,h) of id_X followed by j. Its normalized comparison has source j_!R(id_X)_*K and is invertible on the localizing closure. A generator belongs to that closure by definition. Its source has zero closed restriction by disjoint-support vanishing, hence so does its target. This proves the generator support assertion for every standard admissible coefficient without introducing a new hole.

On each Dctf generator, the closed restriction V F vanishes by the preceding step for standard coefficients. For the separate all-continuous-map compatibility coefficient, [lem-sf-refinement-boundary-vanishing] supplies only the constructible sheaf case in degree zero. Apply the already proved source-library DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded to the triangulated vanishing kernel, using boundedness and constructibility of every homology sheaf, to prove the full generator case. Extend this vanishing to Loc(Dctf) directly: intersect Loc(Dctf) with the kernel of the triangulated functor V F. This intersection contains the generators, is replete, contains zero, is closed under shifts and extensions, and is closed under the relevant ambient sums by the preceding step. The intersection definition of the localizing closure therefore puts every object of Loc(Dctf) in this kernel. The private extend_zero proves each closure assertion, including empty sums. The existing localizingClosure_exists supplies the localizing property of Loc(Dctf).

source.place: (2) Isomorphism, generator calculation and localizing determination applied to a vanishing kernel.

proof.text: For K in the localizing closure, the source of the refinement map has zero closed restriction by the source-library disjoint-support vanishing theorem, and its target does by the preceding step. Its open restriction is invertible: the proved normalization equation writes its composite with the open unit and rho as the other invertible open unit. Cancel these isomorphisms. The source-library theorem jointlyReflectIsomorphisms_leftDerivedUpperStar_of_isCompl, proved from the module open-closed detection on cohomology, now makes the refinement map invertible.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism, open-closed detection after localizing the zero restriction.

proof.text: Normalize the total derived adjunction against the exact-map derived adjunction by comparing counits through rightDerived_ext and the two factorization equations. The source CompConjugate theorem then identifies the specified canonical compositor with the conjugate of the derived exact-pullback triangle comparison. Transport upperStarComp_assoc through mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, whiskering and the associativity of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. The generic restriction_mate_pasting calculation identifies the composite restriction with the restriction of the composite refinement, including the given scheme equality transports. This is the canonical compositor, not an arbitrary choice of isomorphism.

source.place: (3) Identity and transitivity, canonical composition normalization.

proof.text: Apply the open adjunction homEquiv and cancel the two invertible restriction comparisons. Naturality, the restriction pasting equation, and the normalization of each refinement map identify both sides of the desired composition law. For identity, first the invertible open unit makes the open counit invertible on j_!K. Transport it along the canonical derived identity to show the identity-refinement map is invertible. The composition law with both maps identities, together with the canonical derived compositor unit law, identifies its image under the faithful identity direct-image functor with the inverse derived identity. Cancelling gives the stipulated identity equation. The unit law is proved directly from the derived-functor unit factorization, as in the downstream identity module, without importing that consumer.

source.place: (3) Identity and transitivity, for arbitrary unbounded K.

proof_origin.place: H3 stage-3 realization: all four clauses proved by explicit adjunction and compositor normalization, open-closed detection, and the kernel form of localizing determination. Only the independent closed-support calculation on constructible sheaves in degree zero for the all-continuous-map algebraic-closure compatibility coefficient is retained in lem-sf-refinement-boundary-vanishing. The unit route through single-compactification sums, proper base change on generators, and open-closed detection is preserved. Bounded truncation devissage is proved from the existing source-library theorem; the retained boundary assertion has only constructible sheaf inputs in degree zero.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: imported text suppressed the standing scheme/coefficient context required by its own current-blueprint proper-base-change route. Restored the explicit standing k-scheme setting and admissible coefficient module categories. Preserved all three clauses and proved restriction and coherence for arbitrary unbounded K, isomorphism on the ambient localizing closure. Replaced the finite etale-only parenthetical citation by the existing finite/integral/rational proper-base-change statements; added explicit exact adjunction, restriction, cone detection and canonical-composition normalization. No new nodes. No Lean changes or builds.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–2 realize The restriction to X; step 3 realizes (1) Uniqueness; steps 4–7 realize (2) Isomorphism along the same generator/closed-complement/localizing route; steps 8–9 realize (3) Identity and transitivity. The current main-20261015 unit proof is used; the unit record still carries an older master statement.

tool_uses.why: Cartesian coefficients identify immersion module pullback with ordinary inverse image; the compactification unit does not prove this coefficient comparison.
Exact inverse image with identified ring coefficients allows termwise restriction and cohomology detection.
Exact extension by zero, its adjunction/unit, and closed-support vanishing are generic ringed localization facts, not compactification coherence.
The generic complex/homotopy adjunction supplies the unit and counit used to descend the exact open adjunction.
Exact module functors are computed termwise on the unbounded derived category.
Small ringed sites admit functorial K-injective resolutions; this is generic homological algebra.
Open restriction is localization of the pro-etale site, needed for the sectionwise direct-image calculation.
An exact left adjoint implies that open restriction preserves K-injectives, the generic fact invoked by the source.
Quasi-compact open immersions are finite type; this checks the input to the same-unit single-compactification theorem.
Proper base change and composition check geometric hypotheses for the complement and the composite refinement.
Finite-coefficient proper base change on Dctf, exactly the coefficient-specific proper-base-change route of the current unit.
Integral proper base change on Dbc supplies the integral coefficient clause of that same route.
Rational proper base change on Dbc supplies the E and algebraic-closure coefficient clauses of that same route.
Generic module-sheaf zero detection for complementary restrictions, applied to cohomology of the cone.
Generic localizing isomorphism-locus criterion, explicitly required by the current unit route.
Canonical unbounded derived-composition isomorphism and its resolution normalization; supplies no refinement comparison theorem.
